audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers call Trial by Fire a crit passive — 'his barrel poke and passive crit autos', 'passive crit autos chunk you'. It is not a crit and it is not tied to his barrels.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Every few seconds, Gangplank's melee strike will set his opponent on fire.' It is a periodic on-strike burn, so the tell is the timer between his melee hits, not a crit roll. Crit in this matchup comes from his items later, which is a different thing to respect at a different point in the game.
audit.corrected: whys[0] and spikes[0].text now name Trial by Fire and describe it as a periodic burn strike.

audit.whatIsWrong: Remove Scurvy is the ability the whole lane bends around — it is named in nine fields — and its cooldown appears nowhere. Parrrley and Cannon Barrage are never timed either.
audit.why: Remove Scurvy is 22s at rank 1 falling to 14s, Parrrley is 4.5s at every rank, and Cannon Barrage is 160s at rank 1 against Public Execution's 130s. Those three numbers reframe the lane: his poke is permanently available, his cleanse is the one thing worth baiting, and Ambessa gets more ultimates than he does.
audit.corrected: tldr, winCon, phases[1].why, phases[3].why, phases[4].why, breakdown.cooldowns, dontsFull[1].d, dontsFull[2].d, report[5].t and wants.foe[1] now carry the real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Powder Keg is written as something that happens to you — 'eat a full barrel chain', 'his barrel chain keeps you out of auto range'. How a keg actually goes off is never stated.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Gangplank uncovers a powder keg at target location. If he attacks it, it explodes, spreading the attack's damage to enemies in the area, slowing them.' The keg is an object that has to be attacked, and it can be attacked by either player. Breaking it first is not just denial of poke, it is the reason his chain never starts.
audit.corrected: dosFull[0].d, dontsFull[0].d and report[5].t now state that he must attack the keg and that you can break it first.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 2's 'why' claimed 'dash-resets stack your passive shield mid-trade', and Levels 4-5 was the generic 'lane-control window' template while the content layer calls that stage Ambessa's weakest.
audit.why: Drakehound's Step grants bonus attack range, damage, attack speed and an energy refund — no shield; Repudiation is her only shield. At 4-5 her Q is 14-11s and E 13-10s against a 4.5s Parrrley, so he simply pokes for free while she has nothing to answer with.
audit.corrected: phases[1].why and phases[3].why now carry the real numbers and agree with the content layer.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was the generic 'the R lock isolates and finishes the chain — point it at the kill, not the tank'.
audit.why: Cannon Barrage is 160s at rank 1, the longest cooldown in the matchup, against Public Execution's 130s. Ambessa's ultimate comes back first and comes back more often, which is the actual argument for forcing every fight on her R timer rather than saving it.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now compares the two ultimate cooldowns directly.

notes: UNVERIFIED CLAIM I DELIBERATELY LEFT IN PLACE, flag for the user: this matchup asserts four separate times that Remove Scurvy cannot cleanse Ambessa's suppression — 'Remove Scurvy can't cleanse a suppress' in spikes[1] and whys[4], 'Remove Scurvy cleanses CC, but not an active suppression' in mid, and again in wants.you[0]. Riot's Remove Scurvy text is simply 'Eats citrus to cure crowd control effects and restore Health', with no exception written into it, and Ambessa's needsResearch.cleansable is empty, which the brief says means UNKNOWN rather than no. The entire level-6 win condition on this page rests on that exception. I did not edit those strings, per the instruction to leave unverifiable claims alone, but the whole matchup turns on it and it should be checked before this ships. Ambessa's kit file also flags grounding on Repudiation and grounding plus heal on Public Execution; Riot's descriptions contain none of that, so I made no such claim.
